title: The Amazing Squirrel
hook: A part-time superhero in a purple and orange squirrel suit shows up late to a bank robbery. It goes about as well as you'd expect.
blurb: Derek is late. The bank is already robbed. The cops are already sighing. But The Amazing Squirrel has a gliding suit, a goo bomb, a hook gun, and absolutely no plan. When the getaway driver turns out to be a cyborg with a minigun arm, Derek does what he always does — improvises badly, gets lucky, and breaks something important. A short superhero comedy about a guy who is barely qualified to save anyone, including himself.

title: The Correspondent: Origins
hook: A girl, a mask her ex-boyfriend left behind, and a company that sells real superhero equipment to anyone willing to lie about their age.
blurb: Ellie Seymour is seventeen, five feet tall, and working at her parents' hardware store when she discovers that her ex-boyfriend's Halloween mask is an encrypted access key to Acme Hero Equip, Inc. — a company that sells real costumes, real gadgets, and a four-hundred-page manual on how not to get killed. She orders everything she can afford. She lies about her age. She becomes The Correspondent. Then The Rat walks into her father's hardware store, and the wall she's been building between her hero life and her home life comes apart in one night.

title: The Correspondent: Golden Age
hook: A college freshman tries to stay retired from being a costumed vigilante. Her Criminal Justice professor is obsessively hunting The Correspondent — not knowing her student is exactly who she's looking for.
blurb: Ellie retired from being The Correspondent after prom night went sideways. Now she's at Colorado State, trying to be a normal freshman — dorm life, classes, friends. But her girlfriend Shelby has been recruited by Acme Hero Inc., her professor Dr. Bramson is building a case against masked vigilantes, and strange accidents are targeting students on campus. The Freshman Curse has a name: the (Pun)isher. Ellie's retirement is over. She just hasn't admitted it yet.

title: Universal Basic Princess
hook: A crown princess fakes a relationship with an economist after a photo leak. Then it stops being fake.
blurb: When a tabloid photo catches Crown Princess Maren holding hands with an economist at a state dinner, her press team does what press teams do — they run with it. The fake relationship is supposed to last six weeks. Long enough to bury the real story. But Dr. Elin Vargas doesn't read the brief, and Maren has never been good at staying in character.

title: Understudy
hook: A corps ballet dancer and a food truck operator, both stuck in inherited roles, learn to lead their own lives.
blurb: Margot dances in the corps — not because she chose it, but because her mother's name still opens doors at the company. Across the street, Ruth runs a food truck she inherited when her father died, serving the same menu he served, in the same spot, to the same lunch crowd. They meet over a sprained ankle and a bowl of soup. Neither of them is living the life they'd have picked. This is a story about understudies — people standing in someone else's place — and what happens when they step out of the wings.

title: What We Keep
hook: A biological drone built to process the dead keeps a cat instead of killing it. Everything unravels from there.
blurb: On Ibhuma, one of six generation ships carrying the remnants of humanity, Omission-67k has spent three years following protocol without question — until he finds a cat in a dead man's apartment, holds the knife against its chest, and it purrs, and something inside him says no. That refusal cracks open everything he was engineered not to feel. A pet shop owner with a hidden rescue operation. A lost batchmate whose disappearance teaches him what loss means. A ship dying section by section while no one acknowledges it. A quiet science fiction novella about personhood, kindness as subversion, and what defines you when everything you were made for falls apart.

title: Calliope and the Rogue Biologic
hook: A fifteen-year-old clockwork inventor ages out of a grim orphanage and gets a letter to a hero academy. Everyone there knows whose daughter she is.
blurb: Calliope is the daughter of mad scientists, killed by the very monster they created, and everyone at the academy knows it. Aging out of the orphanage with nothing but her wits and a gift for building mechanical solutions, she has to prove she's not doomed to repeat her parents' mistakes. A steampunk YA story about a girl who builds her way out of every corner she's pushed into.

title: Calliope and the Crazed Kraken
hook: A girl with a mechanical hand launches a solo rescue mission 1,600 feet beneath the ocean. Her girlfriend has been running her own intelligence operation from inside the enemy base.
blurb: Calliope's girlfriend Delia has been coerced into attending the Kraken Brotherhood's underwater academy — a militarized mirror-Academy where every discipline serves biologics. The resistance won't risk a rescue for one person. Calliope builds her way down alone: new gear, a stolen airship, a plan held together with schematics and stubbornness. But Delia isn't waiting to be saved. She's been mapping the base, gathering intelligence, and building her own path out. When they reunite in the crushing dark, they discover the Kraken's greatest secret: a biological weapon called the Kraken Mor, and the choice of whether to set it free.

title: Thermal Gradient
hook: Two novellas interleaved — a maintenance engineer and a marine biologist on a dying deep-sea station, told from both sides of the same love story.
blurb: Wren Calder is the sole maintenance technician at Relay Station Aronnax, four hundred meters under the Pacific, where she keeps alive not just the failing station but her terminally ill partner Nico, whose degenerative nerve condition slows under the weight of ocean pressure. When Pelagic Industrial schedules a decommissioning inspection, Wren has to choose between the nine years of work that nobody sees and the one person she cannot measure. A character study in improvised competence and the kind of love that holds onto another person against impossible odds.

title: Closer on Paper
hook: A small-town potion shop owner watches a corporate chain open across the street — and tries to figure out what's worth fighting for.
blurb: Elara has run The Quiet Tincture for years, making potions by hand for people she knows by name. When Verdant Standard opens a branch in Thistlehollow — cheaper prices, standardized formulas, no appointment needed — she has to decide whether what she does is worth enough to survive. It's not good versus evil. Both approaches work. But one of them knows your name, and the other one doesn't need to.

title: Dragon Hoard
hook: A dragon who hoards electronics kidnaps a repair technician to be his damsel. She's furious — until she sees the cave full of broken machines.
blurb: Benjamin hoards electronics. That's what dragons do. He needs a damsel to properly be a dragon, so he kidnaps Alice Huang, a Denver repair technician. Alice is furious until she realizes his cavern of broken machines is an opportunity. Weekdays she works in the city. Weekends she wires jukeboxes and turntables into Benjamin's battery grid. They build something that looks like a life. Then Alice tells her therapist the truth about where she spends her weekends, and the response isn't curiosity — it's psychiatric intervention, forced medication, and a diagnosis that reduces everything real about her life to a symptom.

title: Delta P Mystery
hook: A disgraced PI exiled to an underwater habitat investigates a murdered escort and discovers the caste system everyone lives under isn't biological — it's manufactured.
blurb: Mortimer Stubbs is a private investigator scraping by in Delta P, a deep-sea habitat where social status is written into your skin — or so everyone believes. When a young escort is found drowned in an airlock, her sister hires Stubbs to find answers. What starts as a murder investigation becomes a trail of covered-up worker deaths, a sabotage plot against the habitat's power supply, and a truth that could unravel the entire social order. Classic noir at four hundred meters: everyone's lying, justice costs more than it's worth, and the detective pulls threads anyway.

title: The First of May
hook: A librarian flies home when her father — legendary boss clown Gerrard Kelly — dies at winter quarters. Toxicology says nitroglycerin in his greasepaint.
blurb: Lou Kelly left the circus after high school. She became a librarian. She let the distance grow. When her father turns up dead in his trailer at winter quarters in Estes Park, Colorado, the coroner calls it a heart attack. Lou knows better — the three-nose rotation is wrong, and one nose is missing. Then toxicology comes back: nitroglycerin, absorbed through greasepaint, lethal dose. She partners with Detective Beatrix Sands to work the case. The circus closes ranks. Lou translates the culture; B runs the investigation. Romance simmers beneath the work. And the killer turns out to be the one person nobody was watching.

title: Rio Borealis
hook: A one-armed (the other is cybernetic) saloon keeper on a frontier colony planet moonlights as the town medic. Then she performs an autopsy and the rancher she's cutting open is a robot.
blurb: Lucy runs a saloon in Scobus R8T4, a Martian settlement where she's taken on the town's medical duties and its darkest job: autopsies for the frontier. When a beloved rancher dies in a buggle stampede, her autopsy reveals an impossible truth — he was a robot, and nobody knew, including possibly himself. As Lucy navigates the fallout, she's forced to confront questions about consciousness, identity, and what it means to be human on a hostile planet far from Earth. A space western about a survivor who becomes the hero the town needs.

title: Damsel Protocol
hook: A dragon passed the Damsel Exam and got assigned a captive and a castle. The rescue never came. Eleven years later, neither of them wants it to.
blurb: A dragon passed the exam. Got assigned a damsel. Got assigned a castle. Followed the protocol. Then the rescue never arrived. Eleven years later, the damsel has redecorated, the dragon has learned to cook, and they've built a quiet domestic life out of a bureaucratic arrangement nobody designed for permanence. When a knight finally shows up, neither of them knows what to do with him — or with the fact that the system they've been ignoring still has rules, and the rules say this is supposed to end.

title: What We Built
hook: A man who lied his way onto a generation ship discovers he's dying and has to learn how to actually live.
blurb: Otto got hired to build humanity's exodus vessels by lying about his credentials. Now he's on the generation ship itself with a terminal joint condition, a wife named Bliss who smuggled cats aboard, and a daughter he's raising in the dark between stars. He builds an AI named Susan, confronts the fleet's first crime, and learns that the hardest engineering problem isn't keeping a ship running — it's figuring out how to live when you know the number.

title: What We Found
hook: Children have been disappearing from the fleet for a decade. The investigator drawn by lottery is the woman who smuggled cats aboard at launch. She'll find the pattern. She won't find a way to keep the fleet together after.
blurb: Years after the launch, Bliss is home with Otto and a teenage daughter when the lottery assigns her a case nobody else has connected — children, none of them prominent, vanishing across the fleet over a decade. She grabs the tablet she's carried since the spacewalk and boards a transport. The trail moves between ships that have already started drifting from each other, through a biological research program on the Green Ship that nobody has looked at hard enough, and into a room with the person responsible. They don't deny it. They explain it. They believe what they did was right, and that's worse than a monster. Bliss solves the case. The fleet doesn't survive what she finds.

title: What We Saved
hook: A hundred and fifty years after the launch, two of the six ships are left. The woman who finds her ancestors' tablet learns that everything she was taught is a lie.
blurb: Laura lives on the lower decks of a fleet that doesn't remember it's a fleet. Earth is a myth. The lost ships were 'always lost.' Brother John broadcasts daily and his version of history is the only version. Then Laura salvages an old tablet that holds the combined family record of the first generation — Otto and Bliss's writing, plus the documentation Bliss copied from the Green Ship before the split — and the story she grew up on stops being a story she can believe. She joins a resistance built from people who can't afford to trust each other. She does a spacewalk that nearly kills her. She finds rooms in the ship Brother John didn't know existed. And before the fleet reaches the planet it was always supposed to reach, a small craft appears on sensors carrying a being nobody understands and a colony of cats nobody expected. Six ships left Earth. Two arrived. One sky waits.

title: The Three Fs: Fear, Failure, and Fun
hook: A professional clown with ADHD writes a guide to navigating fear, failure, and fun. Not toxic positivity. Honest survival.
blurb: For twenty years, Dylan has earned a living making people laugh as a professional clown. He's also spent that time managing ADHD, recovering from failure, and discovering that the only antidote to all of it is the ability to play. This isn't a self-help book with solutions. It's a set of tools from someone who's used them to stay alive. From the Ringling audition he failed to the video game that never shipped to the hobby cycle he cycles through endlessly — these are stories about what happens when you stop running from failure and start cycling through it. By the end, you'll know how to do a card trick, and you'll understand why that matters.

title: Portal 5
hook: A struggling Denver stage magician discovers he's the lost fairy prince of Tír na nÓg. The portal is under Denver International Airport, because of course it is.
blurb: Jack Featherstone performs mediocre magic shows at the Denver Clocktower. When his agent arranges for Las Vegas scouts to see his act, Jack's life goes sideways: the scouts are goblins in skin suits, a dragon attacks their limo, and his assistant reveals she's a fairy warrior sent to bring him home. Jack is the lost prince of a dying kingdom, and the portal to save it is under DIA. With nothing but his stage magic and a lifetime of performing for indifferent audiences, he has to fight his way to a throne he never wanted. The best trick he ever learned came from years of nobody clapping.

title: The Rehearsal Dinner
hook: Two families meet. Slime runs the bakery. The story is about learning to eat together.
blurb: Two families sit down to dinner the night before a wedding in Thistlehollow. The food is unfamiliar. The customs don't translate. The baker is a sentient slime mold named Marzipan who makes the best pastry in the valley. A story about coexistence — not the grand gesture kind, but the kind where you try the thing on your plate and say thank you.

title: Filed in Good Faith
hook: A potion shop gets sealed the day before its license renewal. The complaint was filed in good faith. The slime baker across the street has a policy about staying out of regulars' problems. They're a terrible policy-maker.
blurb: Elara Pestle has run The Quiet Tincture for years, mixing custom adjustments for regulars who can't take the standardized stuff. When a regulatory complaint lands the day before her renewal, the seal goes up and the herbs start dying in the window. The clockmaker who filed the complaint did it in good faith — three years of meticulous notes, a statute cited correctly, a sincere belief in safety. But somebody she'd never met sent her the legal summary, picked the date, and is waiting in the gap her closure leaves behind. Marzipan LeFlour, three-pod baker and reluctant noticer, splits across town one regular at a time, follows the paperwork to a name nobody local has heard, and learns that a small town isn't too small to be a target — just too small to notice the hunter.

title: Seen Through
hook: The founding treaty and the last stone of the burned bridge vanish on the same day. Both were kept in spaces only a fogborn could reach. Thistlehollow has one adult fogborn.
blurb: Yolanda Chantal is the obvious suspect. She catalogued both artifacts last month and published their locations. She's the only fogborn in town who could've slipped through the cracks the storage spaces were built to rely on. The town wants this to be about gnome-goblin politics, which is the kind of trouble a town knows how to hold. It isn't. The thief came in on the fish wagon, has been delivering to the dye works for years, and overheard a wedding being planned at LeFlour's bakery. Marzipan LeFlour investigates because Yolanda is a regular, and LeFlour knows regulars. The crime is theft. The motive is heartbreak. The resolution won't pass through a courtroom.

title: Held Ground
hook: Days after the wedding, Orvyn Cragspit doesn't come home. He's the only person in Thistlehollow who has the old goblin mines memorized. Somebody figured that out.
blurb: Pip comes into the bakery alone. He orders his usual. He doesn't order Orvyn's. The empty chair tells LeFlour everything except where to look. A former Verdant Standard contractor has gone freelance, found old survey files, and taken the one Cragspit who carries the family map in his head. What the contractor doesn't know: the mines aren't just mines. They intersect with the convergence that keeps every potion in Thistlehollow working, every fogborn condensed, every enchanted object whole. The Cragspits have tended the dark for generations without naming it. Orvyn will die before he draws a map for the wrong person. Marzipan LeFlour splits two pods underground with Orvyn's grandfather and one pod topside alone — the longest split of their life, the hardest recombination, and the case where the bakery learns what's been holding the floor up the whole time.
